George Masso was born in Cranston, Rhode Island on November 17, 1926.

He played a number of instruments as a youth but was sold on the trombone after hearing Lou McGarity on a Benny Goodman recording. George’s career has embraced the world of education and performing. He received a master’s degree from Boston University and taught music for twenty years in public schools and at the University of Connecticut. In 1973, George took time off to tour with Benny Goodman, and with encouragement from Bobby Hackett, entered the jazz world full time. Since then he has performed and recorded with the World’s Greatest Jazz Band, Woody Herman, Scott Hamilton and numerous others. He is a familiar presence at jazz festivals and parties across the country and he recently released “That Old Gang of Mine” on Arbors Records.
George was interviewed at the Jerome Jazz Party in Aspen, Colorado on October 10, 1997, by Monk Rowe, director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
